issues.legal_issue: The statutory protection for persons occupying specified land applies only when the occupation originated lawfully and does not extend to occupation originating in trespass.
material_facts: The claimant sought deemed-tenant protection based on occupation of land covered by the statutory category of private forests or unsurveyed lands.
The High Court found that the claimant had come into possession by trespass.
The claimant had argued that he owned the land through adverse possession.
issues.conclusion: The phrase “in occupation” means lawful occupation. Because the claimant’s occupation originated in trespass, he was not entitled to the protection; the appeal and special leave petitions were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Reading Section 7D of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, in the context of Sections 7A to 7C and Sections 8 and 9, the Court held that the legislature intended protection for occupation with a lawful origin, including bona fide occupation under mistaken belief, purported leases, or arrangements akin to licences, but not wilful trespass or forcible unlawful entry. Accordingly, “in occupation” in Section 7D means “in lawful occupation.”

predicates.deemed_tenant_protection_sought: A person sought recognition as a tenant based on occupying land.
predicates.covered_land_category: The occupied land fell within the category of land covered by the special deemed-tenancy protection.
predicates.occupation_originated_in_wilful_trespass: The person began occupying the land through wilful trespass or forcible unlawful entry.

issues.definition: When a person seeks deemed-tenant protection for covered land and began occupying it through wilful trespass, that person is not entitled to the protection.
